text:
alex.ng: FYI: we're seeing sustained packet loss in az3b affecting GPU pool-6 — approx 30-40% pod eviction + high retransmits. Investigating. :rotating_light:
infra-bot: [ALERT] packet_loss_high - az3b - 2xx alerts in last 3m - group: gpu-infra
priya.k: thx. are we seeing node failures or just network? any impact on Dedicated customers?
alex.ng: primarily networking between racks. nodes show healthy but kube reports frequent `ReadWriteOnce` mounts flapping and `ImagePullBackOff` spikes. Dedicated SLOs currently within thresholds but tickets incoming.
benji: can we start a soft drain for non-critical pools? I'd prefer we not force-evict Dedicated workloads yet.
maria_g: +1. Recommend `rictl drain-pool --pool gpu-pool-6 --mode soft --exclude dedicated` to cordon and gracefully move jobs. Start scale-up in az3a/az3c.
alex.ng: running: `rictl drain-pool --pool gpu-pool-6 --mode soft --exclude dedicated` — will take ~5-8m to finish eviction
oncall-eng: started proactive scale-up: `asctl scale gpu-pool --region us-west-3 --zones az3a,az3c --add 16 gpus` keep me posted. Also bumping autoscaler headroom to 20%.
network-team: we're seeing inter-rack packet drops pinned to ToR switch firmware queue. Neteng opening TAC with cloud provider. ETA 45-90m for mitigation.
priya.k: what's the expected latency regression for hosted API during this shift? any models at risk of falling back to smaller variants?
benji: estimate p50 latency +8-12ms p95 +40ms for affected routes; if scale-up completes and caching warms, should normalize. We have fallback policy to model-quantized-v2 for long-running sessions.
maria_g: reminder: increase KV cache warmup on new nodes to reduce regen cost. `cachectl warm --target az3a,az3c --promote 10%`
infra-bot: notice: canary rollout active for traffic shift - traffic split updated from 100/0/0 to 60/40 (az3a/az3c) over 10m.
alex.ng: @support-runbook please post a brief note to impacted customers (hosted API latency increase, no data loss). Keep messaging conservative.
support-runbook: posting now to status page and to Dedicated customers in queue. Will include estimated full recovery ETA 2h pending network fix.
benji: cost note: scale-up will add ~120 GPU-hours (spot). If this drags on, switch to reserved nodes for Dedicated to honor SLAs — datacenter procurement needed.
priya.k: ack. keep an eye on spot preemptions. If preemptions >5% in 15m, we'll pivot to reserved and update billing runbook.
alex.ng: drain completed for non-dedicated. 14 of 16 pods moved. Observability shows request success rate stabilized at 98.9% from 96.2%.
network-team: provider reports firmware flaps; mitigations applied to ToR, monitoring for stabilization. Still some packet retransmits but trending down.
oncall-eng: monitoring - p99 errors dropped to baseline, latency trending down. Closing loop, but keeping the pool cordoned until provider confirms.
priya.k: postmortem owners? recommend infra + neteng + runtime. schedule 1h tomorrow to capture action items.
alex.ng: agreed. adding to calendar. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: incident-note: incident-id INF-2026-03-18-az3b - status: mitigated - followup required
